varieties.name: Golden
varieties.note: Gold marbling on green. The quickest grower of the pothos and the most forgiving of a dim corner.

varieties.name: Marble Queen
varieties.note: Heavily white-marbled, so less leaf is doing the work: slower, drinks less, and wants brighter light to keep the variegation.

varieties.name: Snow Queen
varieties.note: Whiter still than Marble Queen, and slower again. Needs the brightest indirect light of the family.

varieties.name: Neon
varieties.note: Plain chartreuse, no variegation. Colour fades toward green in low light rather than reverting.

varieties.name: Jade
varieties.note: Solid green. The most tolerant of low light, since every leaf is working.

varieties.name: N'Joy
varieties.note: Small leaves in clean white and green blocks. Compact and slow; a small pot dries slowly to match.

varieties.name: Pearls and Jade
varieties.note: Small leaves with grey-green and white at the margins. Slow, and prone to crisping in dry air.

varieties.name: Manjula
varieties.note: Wavy leaves with wide cream splashes. Slow, and the cupped leaves hold water: keep it off the foliage.

varieties.name: Global Green
varieties.note: Dark green leaves edged in lighter green. Vigorous for a variegated pothos.

watering.label: Let most of the pot dry before watering again

drainage.label: Free-draining mix; standing wet is the usual cause of loss

established: Too dark. Variegation fades to plain green and the stems run bare between leaves.
Dim. New leaves come small and mostly green; the pale marbling is the first thing lost.
A little short. It grows, but leggy, with more stem than leaf.
Burning. The cream areas go papery first, then dry to tan patches.
Too much. Leaves bleach to pale yellow-white and crisp at the edges.
Far too much. Variegated leaves scorch through within days at this level.
